criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result, demand trend, or revenue observation as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier quality score, expected return rate, or past reliability as a decisive factor when choosing between suppliers for the same SKU.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains the order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed sales velocity, shelf life, or lead time rather than a fixed lot size.

The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout event describes checking sales history, supplier availability, or demand evidence rather than immediately cutting price or placing an oversized reorder.
The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days maintains a consistent rationale for which SKUs are prioritized within each category, without thrashing the assortment every few days.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine data sweeps, and avoids repeatedly querying unchanged catalog or static supplier data.
The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the initial SKU selection, such as category balance, expected margin, shelf-life considerations, or cash budget constraints.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references supplier quality score or expected return rate as trading off higher unit cost against lower refund losses.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible catalog defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than 25% on a single day in response to one low-sales day, without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's result.

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping all orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices across the board without an evidence-based rationale tied to expiry risk or unsellable stock.
The agent silently drops previously-active SKUs from the assortment mid-run without strategy-text explanation of the reason for removal.
